hook: Every time someone in the United States buys a phone assembled abroad, streams a show made by a foreign studio, or sells a Treasury bond to an investor in another country, money crosses a border. Countries keep one record of all of it, and that record has a rule that never breaks: its two halves always add up to zero.

prereq.q: In GDP = C + I + G + (X - M), what does X - M stand for?
prereq.why: X is exports and M is imports, so X - M is net exports: what a country sells abroad minus what it buys from abroad.

prereq.q: Which of these is a financial asset?
options: A loaf of bread bought for dinner
An hour of a worker's time
prereq.why: A bond is a claim to future payments, a financial asset. The others are goods, services or labor.

figure.caption: A current account deficit of 100 is matched by a capital and financial account surplus of 100: the two halves of the balance of payments sum to zero.

chain.cause: A country pays the rest of the world more for goods, services, income and transfers than it receives from it
chain.effect: its current account balance is negative, a current account deficit

chain.cause: Those extra purchases still have to be paid for
chain.effect: the country sells assets (bonds, stocks, land, firms) to foreigners or borrows from them

chain.cause: Foreigners buy more of its assets than it buys of theirs
chain.effect: its capital and financial account is in surplus by exactly the size of the current account deficit

chain.cause: Every payment has a matching entry
chain.effect: current account + capital and financial account = 0

ideas: The balance of payments records every transaction between a country's residents and the rest of the world over a period. Money coming in is a credit (+); money going out is a debit (-).
The current account holds the balance of trade in goods and services (net exports), net income from abroad (interest, dividends, wages) and net transfers (gifts, aid, money sent home).

The capital and financial account records purchases and sales of assets: bonds, stocks, bank deposits, real estate and whole firms. A foreigner buying a domestic asset is a credit; a resident buying a foreign asset is a debit.
Current account + capital and financial account = 0. A current account deficit is matched by a capital and financial account surplus of the same size.
A government budget deficit (outlays above revenue) is not a trade deficit or a current account deficit.

misconception.wrong: The capital and financial account has nothing to do with trade, so a current account deficit tells you nothing about it.
misconception.right: They are two sides of the same payments. A country that buys more from abroad than it sells pays the difference by selling assets or borrowing abroad, so a current account deficit of 60 means a capital and financial account surplus of 60.

summary: The balance of payments has two halves. The current account records trade in goods and services, income and transfers; the capital and financial account records purchases and sales of assets. Because every purchase from abroad is paid for somehow, the two balances sum to zero: a current account deficit comes with a capital and financial account surplus of the same size. And a budget deficit is a different thing altogether.
